The vulnerable code path is absent from the shipped cyrus-sasl2 artifacts. That check is present in the cyrus-sasl 2.1.28 source that Debian packages, and the built libscram plugin in the shipped libsasl2-modules package contains its error message. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-132138

Fixed in this package by backporting the upstream GnuTLS name-constraint corrections (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/6e11fea0d5c5886bd215b81fb35baf10b031c8d8, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/261c718f998351e71db3590a8df78b15961e7e26, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/988f435abdd33c66c75ca2069118e9f1c7fb0206, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/5d1d734f596d89842c7134d5b43c25f45f0306ec), adapted to GnuTLS 3.8.9. Unsupported name constraint types fail closed, and a directoryName constraint rejects any leaf with a non-empty subject DN because DN matching is not implemented. A CA whose permitted directoryName constraint is O=Good rejects a leaf with subject O=Evil, with only the root trusted; the same chain under an unconstrained intermediate is accepted. Verified by runtime tests on the amd64 and arm64 candidates.

Unsupported name constraint types fail closed. A CA constraint on an SRVName (otherName OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.8.7) rejects a leaf that carries an SRVName, and an excluded SRVName constraint rejects the chain even when the leaf carries no SRVName. The same SRVName under an unconstrained CA is accepted. UPN, URI and directoryName constraints are covered by the same tests. Verified by runtime tests on the amd64 and arm64 candidates.

Fixed in github.com/labstack/echo/v4 v4.16.3 (https://github.com/labstack/echo/releases/tag/v4.16.3; advisory https://github.com/labstack/echo/security/advisories/GHSA-246p-cpwv-v3jq). In v4.16.3 Context.RealIP() returns the connection peer address when Echo#IPExtractor is unset instead of trusting client-supplied X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP headers, so rotating forwarded-IP values cannot create fresh default rate-limit buckets. The temporal CLI binary in this image embeds echo/v4 at v4.16.3 or a later release and does not contain the vulnerable pre-fix behavior.

Fixed in github.com/labstack/echo/v4 v4.16.3 (https://github.com/labstack/echo/releases/tag/v4.16.3; advisory https://github.com/labstack/echo/security/advisories/GHSA-99jh-6h7p-pp36). In v4.16.3 the Proxy middleware derives the upstream X-Real-IP header from Context.RealIP(), which uses the connection peer when Echo#IPExtractor is unset, so a client-supplied X-Real-IP is no longer forwarded. The temporal CLI binary in this image embeds echo/v4 at v4.16.3 or a later release and does not contain the vulnerable pre-fix behavior.
